The unique width-fixed critical a follows from a monotone equation. The q=0 quartic coefficient 2c(b_c^2-a_c^2)/(3sqrt(pi)) is positive. Local Taylor inversion yields s^(1/4) at criticality and s^(1/2) away; the implicit-function theorem gives the splitting and norm-gain constants. Entire real-analytic nonconstant multiplier with finitely many monotonic branches has purely absolutely continuous spectrum [0,M] and no eigenvalues. The included standalone standard-library checker passed 128 supplementary finite checks; the proof, rather than numerical tests, establishes the infinite-dimensional statements.
